symptom: A unit test fails at random on one nightly leg, in setup, not in what it tests: `TestCreateMicroflow_NotesRefusedOnFullConstructor` (mdl/backend/mcp) with `copy fixture: open .mxcli/cache/unit-contents.db-journal: no such file or directory`. The same commit passes on every other leg and on re-run
cause: A cross-package race on the checked-in fixtures, not a product defect. Since the unit-contents store (ako/mxcli#1804) any reader that opens a project writes `.mxcli/cache/unit-contents.db` next to it, and tests that open testdata/expr-checker, testdata/pedapp or modelsdk/mpr/testdata/v1-project in place write it into the fixture; its SQLite journal appears and disappears with each write. go test runs packages in parallel, so another package's whole-directory `os.CopyFS` (25 tests) or hand-written walk listed the journal and then failed to open it. Nothing under a fixture's .mxcli is tracked
file: `internal/testutil/fixture.go` (`CopyFixture`: os.CopyFS over a view that hides every .mxcli), used by every whole-fixture copy in tests, and by cmd/mxcli's copyTree and copyFixtureTree
insight: A cache that writes next to the project turns every checked-in fixture into shared mutable state between test packages; any whole-directory copy of one is then a race whose odds grow with the suite. Copy what the fixture commits, never its .mxcli, which also makes the copy what a fresh checkout holds whichever tests ran first (exec_atomic's hashTree already ignored .mxcli for the same reason). After a full `make test`, `find . -name .mxcli -path '*testdata*'` lists the fixtures being written in place. The race is reproduced deterministically by an fs.FS whose listing names a journal that Open reports missing: plain os.CopyFS fails with the nightly's error, CopyFixture copies; with its filter stubbed it fails the same way
